L2t: India and the Soviet Union established diplomatic relations in 1947, and India's early ambassadors to Moscow were chosen from outside the regular diplomatic service.
L3t: India's first ambassador to Moscow after independence was a renowned philosopher and Oxford professor who later became Vice President and then President of India.
L4t: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the philosopher-scholar who later became India's Vice President and President, served as India's Ambassador to the Soviet Union from 1949 to 1952.
L2f: India's ambassadors to Moscow in the early years after independence were all career officers of the Indian Civil Service who had served in Europe.
L3f: The post of Ambassador to the Soviet Union in 1949 was held by Jawaharlal Nehru's sister, who had just completed her term as India's envoy in Washington and was moved to Moscow.
L4f: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was India's Ambassador to the Soviet Union from 1949 to 1952.
